title: Philippine Habitat and Ecology Reference
reviewLevel: Source-based field descriptions, not a formally validated Philippine habitat classification key
scope: General descriptions to help document actual sites; absence of habitat observations does not imply species absence.

sources.title: Philippine Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan 2024–2040, DAO 2025-23: Philippine forest formations

profiles.name: Lowland tropical forest
profiles.overview: Warm, humid forest on lower slopes and plains. Canopy composition, disturbance history and terrain vary widely across Philippine islands. Old-growth and regenerating stands should be recorded separately.
profiles.fieldIndicators: Record connected canopy, vertical tree layers, mature stems, lianas, saplings and understory density. Measure canopy openness rather than calling all closed cover old-growth.
profiles.waterAndSubstrate: Assess slope position, drainage, nearby streams, erosion signs and soil surface. Elevation alone does not define the habitat boundary.
profiles.vegetationAndWildlife: Tree community and understory structure reflect geology, rainfall and land use. Record birds, mammals, herpetofauna and plant observations independently.
profiles.limitations: Forest boundaries are gradual and locally variable. Avoid automatic elevations as a definition of lowland forest.

profiles.name: Montane forest
profiles.overview: Upland forest along mountain gradients, often cooler and wetter than nearby lowlands. Changes in tree community and canopy structure can occur gradually rather than at one fixed contour.
profiles.fieldIndicators: Note canopy height, tree-stature shifts, epiphyte abundance and understory layering. Record sampling locality and exposure.
profiles.waterAndSubstrate: Observe ridge versus ravine, mist/cloud exposure, water seepage and surface soil. Do not infer climatic values from altitude.
profiles.vegetationAndWildlife: Plant community differs between mountain ranges and parent materials. Document actual trees and epiphytes where identifiable.
profiles.limitations: Submontane, montane and mossy forest should not be separated by arbitrary universal altitude limits.

profiles.name: Mossy / upper montane forest
profiles.overview: Cool, frequently wet upland forest often characterized by short or contorted trees and abundant mosses, lichens and epiphytes. It occurs across varied elevations depending on mountain climate.
profiles.fieldIndicators: Record moss and bryophyte cover on branches and stems, stature of the canopy, epiphyte abundance and exposure. Avoid labeling every high-elevation grassland as mossy forest.
profiles.waterAndSubstrate: Document mist frequency, ridgeline position, organic-rich litter, saturated substrates and water movement when actually observed.
profiles.vegetationAndWildlife: Often supports specialized upland flora and fauna. The profile describes habitat structure, not automatic endemic-species presence.
profiles.limitations: Disturbance and local climate alter structure. Confirm mossy features on the ground.

profiles.name: Limestone and karst forest
profiles.overview: Forests on limestone-derived terrain with outcrops, cliffs, pinnacles, fissures or caves. Vegetation structure varies strongly over short distances with rock exposure and soil pockets.
profiles.fieldIndicators: Document exposed limestone, sinkholes, crevices, thin soils, abrupt microtopography and cliff habitat. Note forest cover separately.
profiles.waterAndSubstrate: Record surface runoff paths, cave moisture and dry rock crevices without entering unsafe voids. Substrate-specific microhabitats matter.
profiles.vegetationAndWildlife: Karst flora may show substrate specialization. Cave and cliff observations require separate search effort and disturbance notes.
profiles.limitations: A species occurring in karst forest is not necessarily a limestone specialist. Confirm rock type rather than assuming it from vegetation.

profiles.name: Ultramafic / ultrabasic forest
profiles.overview: Vegetation established on rock and soils formed from ultramafic materials. Plant communities may differ markedly from neighboring non-ultramafic forests.
profiles.fieldIndicators: Describe substrate exposure, vegetation stature, leaf characteristics, patchiness and transitions into other soil types.
profiles.waterAndSubstrate: Record drainage, bare-rock patches and soil color. Chemical soil identity requires an actual geologic or laboratory source.
profiles.vegetationAndWildlife: Possible local plant community specialization. Wildlife use must be documented directly, not inferred from underlying rock.
profiles.limitations: Do not assign ultramafic habitat from small-tree stature alone. Separate field impression from verified geology.

profiles.name: Mangrove forest and tidal woodland
profiles.overview: Tree and shrub communities in tidal intertidal and brackish coastal settings. They can follow sheltered mudflats, estuaries and tidal river channels.
profiles.fieldIndicators: Look for tidal influence, prop roots or pneumatophores, salt-tolerant woody vegetation, muddy or sandy intertidal zones. Record the precise microzone.
profiles.waterAndSubstrate: Note inundation state, approximate tidal position, salinity reading if measured, standing water and sediment type.
profiles.vegetationAndWildlife: Common mangrove genera include Rhizophora, Avicennia and Bruguiera. Root networks support many invertebrates, fish and coastal birds.
profiles.limitations: Planted stands and natural forest differ. One photograph does not confirm exact salinity or plant identity.

profiles.name: Freshwater marsh and wetland
profiles.overview: Inland or coastal freshwater-influenced wetlands with seasonally or permanently saturated soils and standing or slow-moving water. Vegetation ranges from emergent plants to sedge and grass communities.
profiles.fieldIndicators: Record the dominant growth form, permanent or seasonal flooding, open-water patches and water-edge transitions.
profiles.waterAndSubstrate: Measure water depth and field conductivity or salinity when feasible. Document water clarity, flow, mud or organic substrate and seasonality.
profiles.vegetationAndWildlife: Anuran calls, waterbirds and aquatic species should be associated with actual observation records and sampling effort.
profiles.limitations: A one-day observation cannot determine permanent hydroperiod. Do not equate absence of water with habitat absence.

profiles.name: Riparian forest and stream margin
profiles.overview: Vegetation along streams and river corridors where flood, streamflow and local moisture influence the edge environment. Can occur within lowland, montane or disturbed landscapes.
profiles.fieldIndicators: Identify channel, banks, riparian canopy, flood marks, erosion and vegetation transition. Record whether the survey is in-channel, bank-edge or adjacent forest.
profiles.waterAndSubstrate: Measure stream width, wetted width, water depth, flow class, channel substrate and sampling-bank distance.
profiles.vegetationAndWildlife: Stream-associated amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals may use different microhabitats. Record detections by observed substrate.
profiles.limitations: Riparian is a landscape position and can coexist with another forest category. No assumed water chemistry.

profiles.name: Secondary forest and disturbed mosaic
profiles.overview: Vegetation recovering from logging, burning, cultivation, storms or other disturbance. This category includes diverse successional stages and should not be treated as one uniform forest type.
profiles.fieldIndicators: Record canopy regeneration, planted versus native vegetation, stumps, trail/road edges, gaps, invasive plants and nearby land use.
profiles.waterAndSubstrate: Document drainage modifications, exposed soil, erosion, water channels and fire evidence.
profiles.vegetationAndWildlife: Mixed natural regeneration and planted trees can coexist. Describe actual vegetation rather than an unverified 'pristine' status.
profiles.limitations: Forest cover alone does not quantify ecological integrity. Classify disturbance and forest structure independently.

profiles.name: Tropical subalpine rainforest
profiles.overview: High-elevation Philippine forest formation recognized in DENR's twelve-formation classification. It differs from lower-elevation montane forest; measure the plant community, exposure and tree stature rather than assigning this name from an altitude alone.
profiles.fieldIndicators: Record canopy stature, exposure, woody plant forms, patches of shrub and canopy, observed mist, and local habitat transitions. Do not infer a subalpine forest solely from a high GPS elevation.
profiles.waterAndSubstrate: Measure rock exposure, drainage, organic horizon, wind exposure and slope position where safe and feasible.
profiles.vegetationAndWildlife: Record actual plant taxa and structure, not a predicted set of associated vertebrates. The existence of this forest formation does not imply local presence of a particular mammal or bird.
profiles.limitations: Elevation bands differ across mountains and islands. Require field vegetation evidence and cite the source classification, not an assumed national elevation threshold.

profiles.name: Beach forest / coastal strand woodland
profiles.overview: Coastal forest on land above usual tidal inundation, separately named from mangrove woodland in DENR forest formations.
profiles.fieldIndicators: Look for woody beach or backshore vegetation on sand or coastal shingle landward of the active swash. Document erosion, tourism, plantation history and natural regeneration.
profiles.waterAndSubstrate: Record sand, shell or shingle substrate and salt-spray exposure. Do not mark tide-washed intertidal mangrove mud as beach forest.
profiles.vegetationAndWildlife: Record coastal trees only after identification. Beach plant lists depend on local island, exposure and human modification.
measurements: Evidence of salt spray and tide reach
profiles.limitations: Beach forest and planted coconut belts are not equivalent. Verify natural woody assemblages and site history.

profiles.name: Freshwater swamp forest
profiles.overview: Freshwater waterlogged forest formation in the national classification. Distinct from an open freshwater marsh by the presence of a woody forest canopy.
profiles.fieldIndicators: Record woody canopy, standing freshwater or saturating soils, water-level marks, and roots exposed to periodic inundation.
profiles.waterAndSubstrate: Check freshwater source, seasonality, organic or mineral substrate, and presence of drains, tidal mixing or upstream floodwater.
profiles.vegetationAndWildlife: Document actual woody plants and epiphytes, plus wildlife observations independently. A wetland label does not establish wildlife occupancy.
measurements: Water depth and recent flood level
profiles.limitations: A flooded plantation, saltwater mangrove or open marsh is not automatically freshwater swamp forest. Seasonal field conditions must be documented.

profiles.name: Peat swamp forest
profiles.overview: Peat swamp is recognized as a separate forest formation from freshwater mineral-soil swamp. Peat consists of accumulated organic material in waterlogged conditions.
profiles.fieldIndicators: Look for forested waterlogged soils and substantial organic soil layers. Do not label a black-colored wetland peat without appropriate soil evidence.
profiles.waterAndSubstrate: Record peat depth where sampling is authorized, water table, drainage, organic substrate, and any evidence of burning or drying.
profiles.vegetationAndWildlife: Record actual forest vegetation and any special substrate-associated plants. Habitat photographs alone cannot confirm a deep peat profile.
profiles.limitations: Peat requires substrate evidence, not appearance alone. Distinguish shallow organic topsoil on mineral deposits from peat.

profiles.name: Tropical semi-evergreen rainforest
profiles.overview: A Philippine forest formation recognized separately from always-green lowland rainforest and tropical moist deciduous forest.
profiles.fieldIndicators: Record actual canopy phenology, evergreen and seasonal leaf-shedding tree components, tree layering, and the time of year sampled.
profiles.waterAndSubstrate: Document local seasonality, drainage and soil type rather than assigning rainfall and drought values without measurements.
profiles.vegetationAndWildlife: Record canopy leaf condition and identified tree taxa across seasons. A dry-looking canopy in one visit is not sufficient for classification.
profiles.limitations: Leaf loss may reflect disturbance, pests or short droughts. Repeat or historical vegetation evidence is needed to separate formation from adjacent types.

profiles.name: Tropical moist deciduous forest
profiles.overview: A seasonally leaf-shedding tropical forest type included in the Philippine twelve-formation national overview.
profiles.fieldIndicators: Document seasonal leaf shedding in naturally established forest and mature tree structure, distinguishing it from recently cleared or damaged evergreen forests.
profiles.waterAndSubstrate: Record soil, drainage, landform and seasonal moisture conditions. Do not infer climate from a single dry field visit.
profiles.vegetationAndWildlife: Note confirmed deciduous and evergreen components, stand history and wildlife detections separately.
profiles.limitations: A defoliated secondary stand is not automatically a natural deciduous forest. Published formation criteria and seasonal records should guide classification.
